name: Spite and Malice
description: Spite and Malice (also known as Cat and Mouse) is a competitive patience game for two or more players, traditionally played with two or more standard decks of cards. It is the direct ancestor of the commercial game Skip-Bo. The objective is to be the first to move all cards from your personal 'pay-off pile' onto center 'build piles'. Kings are wild (or Jokers), and Aces start the piles.

content.text: Spite and Malice (also known as Cat and Mouse) is a competitive patience game for two or more players, traditionally played with two or more standard decks of cards. It is the direct ancestor of the commercial game Skip-Bo. The objective is to be the first to move all cards from your personal 'pay-off pile' onto center 'build piles'. Kings are wild (or Jokers), and Aces start the piles.
Derived from Russian Bank (Crapette) principles but simpler. 'Spite' refers to blocking opponents.

Shuffle both packs together. Deal 20 cards face down to each player's pay-off pile and 5 cards to each player's hand. Place the remainder face down as the stock. Turn the top card of each pay-off pile face up. The player with the higher pay-off card plays first (if equal, shuffle pay-off and turn a new top card).

items.text: Unlimited center stacks: Allow unlimited center stacks; completed stacks removed only when stock is depleted.
Compulsory play of aces: Aces must be played as soon as drawn or when on top of pay-off or side stack; no limit on number of center stacks.
Scoring: Winner scores 5 plus one per card left in opponent's pay-off pile; stalemate: score difference. Play to target (e.g. 50).
